machine.CPU: 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-11390H @ 3.40GHz (4 cores / 8 threads)

settings.name: autovacuum
settings.why: keeps statistics fresh; demo 01 turns it off for its own table to show stale statistics

settings.name: checkpoint_timeout
settings.why: checkpoint interval; a checkpoint during a case can add write time

settings.name: effective_cache_size
settings.why: planner's guess of total cache (shared_buffers + OS); higher favours index scans

settings.name: jit
settings.why: compiles expressions of large queries; adds start-up time to big aggregates (11, 14)

settings.name: maintenance_work_mem
settings.why: index build speed; the demos set 1 GB in their own session

settings.name: max_parallel_workers
settings.why: parallel workers available to all queries (demo 14)

settings.name: max_parallel_workers_per_gather
settings.why: workers per query: parallel scans in 04, 06, 11, 17; varied 0-6 in demo 14

settings.name: max_wal_size
settings.why: checkpoint distance; matters for index builds and bulk writes

settings.name: random_page_cost
settings.why: 4 is the spinning-disk default; on NVMe ~1.1 is common and shifts plans to index scans

settings.name: shared_buffers
settings.why: PostgreSQL's cache: decides 'hit' vs 'read' in every plan (demos 00, 12)

settings.name: synchronous_commit
settings.why: each commit waits for the WAL flush; affects the insert cases (07, 10, 20)

settings.name: track_io_timing
settings.why: adds I/O read time to BUFFERS output and pg_stat_statements

settings.name: work_mem
settings.why: per sort / hash step; top-N sorts and aggregates (01, 07, 11) fit in 4 MB here

method.Timing: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT JSON), median of 5 runs (3 when the first run takes over 2 s); first run reported separately
method.Client timing: psql wall clock, results discarded, minus psql start-up (22 ms, measured each run)
method.Isolation: each demo creates its own indexes/tables and drops them afterwards; data-changing cases run in BEGIN ... ROLLBACK
